answer: The driller reads the temperature at every depth of the borehole, and the log is signed by the driller and the engineer who watched the gauge. A inlet log written ashore fails the check: at the tide of the hole the temperatures must rise exactly as the earth heats them, and a written log guesses wrong. Buying a false log means bribing the driller, faking a drilling run and paying 31,000, and the grove record in the drilling office is kept for the life of the borehole, so a second borehole claiming the same log is sealed.
